τρυγάω, -ῶ [in LXX for קָצַר, בָּצַר, etc. ;] to gather in: with accusative, (a) of the fruit, [[luke 6 44|Luk.6:44]], [[revelation 14 18|Rev.14:18]]; (b) of that from which it is gathered, [[revelation 14 19|Rev.14:19.]]† (AS)

τρυμαλιά, -ᾶς, ἡ (τρύω, to wear away), [in LXX: [[jeremiah 13 4|Jer.13:4]] (נָקִיק), etc. ;] = τρύμη, a hole: τ. ῥαφίδος, eye of a needle, [[mark 10 25|Mrk.10:25.]]† SYN.: τρῆμα, τρύπημα (AS)
τρύπημα, -τος, τό (τρυπάω, to bore) a hole: τ. ῥαφιδος, eye of a needle, [[matthew 19 24|Mat.19:24]] (WH, txt., τρῆμα).† SYN.: τρῆμα, τρυμαλιά (AS)
Τρύφαινα, -ης, ἡ Tryphæna: [[romans 16 12|Rom.16:12]] (see Lft., Phi., 175 f.; MM, xxv).† (AS)

τρυφάω, -ῶ (τρυφή), [in LXX: [[nehemiah 9 25|Neh.9:25]] (עָדַן hithp.), [[isaiah 66 11|Isa.66:11]] (עָנַג hithp.), Sir.14:4 * ;] to live daintily, luxuriously, to fare sumptuously: [[james 5 5|Jas.5:5]] (cf. ἐν-τρυφάω).† SYN.: σπαταλάω (which see), στρηνιάω (AS)
τρυφή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for עָדַן ;] softness, daintiness, luxuriousness: [[luke 7 25|Luk.7:25]], [[2-peter 2 13|2Pe.2:13]].† (AS)
Τρυφῶσα, -ης, ἡ, ς, ἡ Tryphosa: [[romans 16 12|Rom.16:12]] (see Lft., Phi., 175 f.).† (AS)
Τρῳάς (Rec. Τρω-), -άδος, ἡ Troas, a city near the Hellespont: [[acts 16 8|Act.16:8, 11 20:5-6]], [[2-corinthians 2 12|2Co.2:12]], [[2-timothy 4 13|2Ti.4:13]].† (AS)
Τρωγύλλιον (also written -γύλιον, -γίλιον, -ία, see Bl., § 6, 3), -ου Trogyllium, a city of Ionia: [[acts 20 15|Act.20:15]] (WH, txt., R, txt., om.).† (AS)

τρώγω 1. prop., of animals, to gnaw, munch, crunch (Hom., al.). 2. Of men, to eat raw food, as vegetables, nuts, etc. (Hdt., al.). 3. In late vernacular, simply to eat (= ἐσθίω): [[matthew 24 38|Mat.24:38]], [[john 6 54|Jhn.6:54, 56-58 13:18]] (LXX ἐσθίων) (see Kennedy, Sources, 82, 155; MM, xxv).† (AS)

τυγχάνω [in LXX: [[deuteronomy 19 5|Deu.19:5]] (מָצָא), [[job 3 21|Job.3:21 7:2 17:1]], [[proverbs 30 23|Pro.30:23]] (without definite Heb. equiv.), Wis.15:19, 1Ma.11:42, 3Ma.3:7, al. ;] I. Trans. 1. to hit (opposite to ἁμαρτάνω, to miss the mark: Hom., Xen., al.). 2. to hit upon, light upon; (a) of persons, to meet with, fall in with: absol., ptcp., ὁ τυχών, a chance person, anyone (Lat. quivis), οὐ τυχών, not common or ordinary, [[acts 19 11|Act.19:11 28:2]]; (b) of things, to reach, get, obtain: with genitive of thing(s) [[luke 20 35|Luk.20:35]], [[acts 24 3|Act.24:3 26:22 27:3]], [[2-timothy 2 10|2Ti.2:10]] [[hebrews 8 6|Heb.8:6 11:35]]. II. Intrans., to happen; of things, to happen, chance, befall: impers., εἰ τύχοι, it may be, perhaps, [[1-corinthians 14 10|1Co.14:10 15:37]]; so ptcp., τυχόν (old accusative absol.; see M, Pr., 74), [[1-corinthians 16 6|1Co.16:6]] (cf. ἐν-, ὑπερ-εν-, ἐπι-, παρα-, συν-τυγχάνω).† τυχόν, adv., see: τυγχάνω (AS)

τυμπανίζω (τύμπανον, a kettle-drum), [in LXX: [[1-samuel 21 13|1Ki.21:13]] (14) (17 pi?) * ;] 1. to beat a drum. 2. to torture by beating, beat to death (cf. Westc. on He, l.with): pass., [[hebrews 11 35|Heb.11:35.]]† (AS)

τύπος, -ου, ὁ (τύπτω), [in LXX: [[exodus 25 39|Exo.25:39]] (40) (תַּבְנִית), [[amos 5 26|Amo.5:26]], 3Ma.3:30, 4Ma.6:19 * ;] 1. the mark of a blow: τῶν ἥλων, [[john 20 25|Jhn.20:25.]] 2. An impression, impress, the stamp made by a die; hence, a figure, image: [[acts 7 43|Act.7:43]] (LXX). 3. form (Plat.): [[romans 6 17|Rom.6:17;]] the sense or substance of a letter (3Mac, l.with), [[acts 23 25|Act.23:25.]] 4. an example, pattern: [[acts 7 44|Act.7:44]], [[hebrews 8 6|Heb.8:6]]" (LXX) ; in ethical sense, [[philippians 3 17|Php.3:17]], [[1-thessalonians 1 7|1Th.1:7]], [[2-thessalonians 3 9|2Th.3:9]], [[1-timothy 4 12|1Ti.4:12]], [[titus 2 7|Tit.2:7]], [[1-peter 5 3|1Pe.5:3]]; in doctrinal sense, type (see ICC, in l), [[romans 5 14|Rom.5:14.]]† τυπικῶς, adv. (τύπος), (a) typically (Greg. Naz.) (b) by way of example: [[1-corinthians 10 11|1Co.10:11.]]† SYN.: see: ὑποτύπωσις (AS)

τύπτω [in LXX chiefly for hi. ;] to strike, smite, beat: with accusative, [[matthew 24 49|Mat.24:49]], [[mark 15 19|Mrk.15:19]], [[luke 12 45|Luk.12:45]], [[acts 18 17|Act.18:17 21:32 23:2-3]]; of mourners, τὰ στήθη, [[luke 18 13|Luk.18:13 23:48]]; ἐπὶ τ. σιαγόνα, [[luke 6 29|Luk.6:29;]] εἰς τ. κεφαλήν, [[matthew 27 30|Mat.27:30.]] Metaphorical, of God inflicting evil: [[acts 23 3|Act.23:3]] (cf. [[exodus 8 2|Exo.8:2]], [[ezekiel 7 9|Eze.7:9]], al.); of disquieting conscience, [[1-corinthians 8 12|1Co.8:12.]]† (AS)

1. an absolute sovereign , unlimited by law or constitution, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: not applied to old hereditary sovereignties βασιλεῖαι); such as those of (Homer) or of Sparta; for the term rather regards the irregular way in which the power was gained , than the way in which it was exercised , being applied to the mild Pisistratus, but not to the despotic kings of Persia. However, the word soon came to imply reproach, like our tyrant , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 2. in a wider sense, the tyrant's son , or any member of his family , (Sophocles Tragicus):—;so, ἡ τύραννος was both the queen herself or a princess , (Euripides) 3. τύραννος, ον, as adjective kingly, royal , [variant datesTragica Adespota 4. imperious, despotic , (Thucydides); τύραννα δρᾶν (Sophocles Tragicus) τύραννος is probably from same Root as κύριος, κοίρανος. (ML)
τυρβάζω to disturb, trouble: pass., [[luke 10 41|Luk.10:41]], Rec. (WH, R, θορυβάζω).† (AS)
of Tyre, Tyrian , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

Τύρος, -ου, ἡ Tyre, a maritime city of Phænicia: [[mark 7 31|Mrk.7:31]], [[acts 21 3|Act.21:3]], 7; Τ. κ, Σιδών, [[matthew 11 21|Mat.11:21-22 15:21]], [[mark 3 8|Mrk.3:8 7:24]], [[luke 6 17|Luk.6:17 10:13-14]].† (AS)

τυφλός, -ή, -όν [in LXX for עִוֵּר ;] blind: as subst., ὁ τ., [[matthew 9 27|Mat.9:27]], [[mark 8 22|Mrk.8:22]], [[luke 4 18|Luk.4:18]]" (LXX), [[john 5 3|Jhn.5:3]], al. Metaphorical: [[matthew 15 14|Mat.15:14 23:16-26]], [[john 9 39|Jhn.9:39-41]], [[romans 2 19|Rom.2:19]], [[2-peter 1 9|2Pe.1:9]], [[revelation 3 17|Rev.3:17]]. (AS)

τυφλόω, -ῶ (τυφλός), [in LXX: [[isaiah 42 19|Isa.42:19]] (עִוֵּר), Tob.7:7 א, Wis.2:21 א * ;] to blind, make blind: metaphorically, [[john 12 40|Jhn.12:40]] (LXX, καμμύω), [[2-corinthians 4 4|2Co.4:4]], [[1-john 2 11|1Jn.2:11]].† (AS)

τυφόω, -ῶ (τῦφος, smoke; metaphorically, conceit), prop., to wrap in smoke; used only metaphorically, to puff up, becloud with pride: pass., [[1-timothy 3 6|1Ti.3:6 6:4]], [[2-timothy 3 4|2Ti.3:4]] (Dem., Arist., al.).† (AS)
τύφω (τῦφος, smoke), to raise a smoke; pass., to smoke: [[matthew 12 20|Mat.12:20]] (LXX, καπνιζόμενον).† (AS)
τυφωνικός, -ή, -όν (τῦφων, a hurricane, typhoon) tempestuous: [[acts 27 14|Act.27:14.]]† (AS)
τύχικος (T, Rec., Τυχικός), -ου, ὁ Tychicus: [[acts 20 4|Act.20:4]], [[ephesians 6 21|Eph.6:21]], [[colossians 4 7|Col.4:7]], [[2-timothy 4 12|2Ti.4:12]], [[titus 3 12|Tit.3:12]].† (AS)

ὑακίνθινος, -η, -ον (ὑάκινθος), [in LXX for תַּחַשׁ, תְּכֵלֶת ;] of hyacinth, hyacinthine (see: ὑάκινθος), "doubtless meant to describe the blue smoke of a sulphurous flame" (Swete): [[revelation 9 17|Rev.9:17]] (Hom., Eur., al.).† (AS)

ὑακίνθος, -ου, ό [in LXX chiefly for תְּכֵלֶת ;] hyacinth; (a) in cl., a flower, prob. the dark blue iris; (b) in late writers, a precious stone of the same colour, perhaps the sapphire: [[revelation 21 20|Rev.21:20]] (Phil., FlJ, al.).† (AS)
ὑάλινος, -η, -ον (ὕαλος), of glass, glassy [[revelation 4 6|Rev.4:6 15:2]].† (AS)
ὕαλος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: [[job 28 17|Job.28:17]] (זְכוּכִית) * ;] 1. (Hdt.) a clear transparent stone. 2. (from Plat. on) glass: [[revelation 21 18|Rev.21:18, 21]].† (AS)

ὑβρίζω (ὕβρις), [in LXX for גֵּאֶה, etc. ;] 1. intrans., to wax wanton, run riot. 2. Trans., to outrage, insult, treat insolently: with accusative of person(s), [[matthew 22 6|Mat.22:6]], [[luke 11 45|Luk.11:45 18:32]], [[acts 14 5|Act.14:5]], [[1-thessalonians 2 2|1Th.2:2]].† (AS)

ὕβρις, -εως, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for גָּאוֹן and cogn. forms ;] 1. wantonness, insolence. 2. = ὕβρισμα, an act of wanton violence, an outrage, injury: [[2-corinthians 12 10|2Co.12:10;]] metaphorically, of a loss by sea (find.), [[acts 27 10|Act.27:10, 21]] (see MM, xxv).† (AS)

ὑβριστής, -οῦ, ὁ (ὑβρίζω), [in LXX chiefly for גֵּאֶה ;] a violent, insolent man: [[romans 1 20|Rom.1:20]], [[1-timothy 1 13|1Ti.1:13]] (EV, injurious).† SYN.: ἀλαζών, ὑπερήφανος, see Tr., Syn., § xxix (AS)

ὑγιαίνω (ὑγιής), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלוֹם, and frequently in To ;] to be sound, healthy, in good health: [[luke 5 31|Luk.5:31 7:10 15:27]], 3Jo.2. In Past. Epp. (as also in cl.) metaphorically, ὑ. ἐν τ. πίστει, [[titus 1 13|Tit.1:13]] ; τ. πίστει, τ. ἀγάπῃ, τ. ὑπομονῇ, [[titus 2 2|Tit.2:2;]] ἡ ὑγιαίνουσα διδασκαλία, [[1-timothy 1 10|1Ti.1:10]], [[2-timothy 4 3|2Ti.4:3]], [[titus 1 9|Tit.1:9 2:1]] ; λόγοι ὑγιαίνοντες, [[1-timothy 6 3|1Ti.6:3]], [[2-timothy 1 13|2Ti.1:13]].† (AS)

ὑγιής, -ές, accusative, ὑγιῆ (Attic usually -ιᾶ), [in LXX for חַי, etc. ;] sound, whole, healthy: [[matthew 12 13|Mat.12:13 15:31]], Jhn.5:[4], 6, 9, 11, 14, 15 7:23, [[acts 4 10|Act.4:10]]; before ἀπό, [[mark 5 34|Mrk.5:34;]] of words, opinions, etc. (as in cl.), metaphorically, λόγος, [[titus 2 8|Tit.2:8.]]† (AS)
